content: Before starting lansoprazole, your healthcare provider will need to determine if it is appropriate for you. You should inform them about your current and past health conditions, including any of the following: Low blood potassium levels (hypokalemia) Low blood magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia) Low blood calcium levels (hypocalcemia) Low blood sodium levels (hyponatremia) Liver problems Phenylketonuria (PKU) Additionally, you should disclose all medications and supplements you are currently taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements. Lansoprazole may interact with these substances, so it is important to provide a complete list to your healthcare provider. Refer to the Interactions section for more details. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding It is not known whether lansoprazole can affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. They will advise you on whether you should take lansoprazole during pregnancy. Do not take lansoprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions Lansoprazole should be taken before meals. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects lansoprazole. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are using. Certain drugs may interact with lansoprazole, including: Methotrexate (used for cancer and autoimmune diseases) Digoxin (used for irregular heartbeat and heart failure) Warfarin (a blood thinner) Theophylline (used for lung diseases) Clarithromycin (an antibiotic) Tacrolimus (used to prevent organ transplant rejection) Certain antiretroviral medications for HIV/AIDS, such as rilpivirine, nelfinavir, or saquinavir St. John’s Wort Rifampin (used for tuberculosis) Some medications may alter the blood levels of lansoprazole, and vice versa. Always provide a full list of medications to your healthcare provider. Overdose and Missed Doses If you or someone else has taken too much lansoprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Side Effects Common Side Effects Diarrhea Stomach pain Nausea Constipation If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here. Contact your provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. Serious Side Effects 1. Kidney Problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis can occur at any time during treatment. If you notice decreased urine output or blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your provider if these occur. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Rare but serious conditions like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) can occur. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes, blisters, or red, watery eyes. Stop taking lansoprazole and seek emergency help if these symptoms develop. 4. DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms): This severe allergic reaction can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin/eyes (jaundice). Stop the medication and seek immediate medical attention if these occur. 5. Lupus: Lansoprazole can cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Inform your provider if these occur. 6. Vitamin B12 Deficiency: Long-term use (3 years or more) can reduce vitamin B12 absorption, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. Contact your provider if these occur. 7. Hypomagnesemia: Lansoprazole can cause low magnesium levels, which may lead to seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Stop the medication and contact your provider if these occur. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term or high-dose use, especially in older adults, may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures. Precautions Who Should Not Use Lansoprazole? Individuals allergic to lansoprazole, any proton pump inhibitor (PPI), or any ingredients in the specific product should not use it. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the product. General Guidelines Do not take lansoprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as directed. Do not share lansoprazole with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep lansoprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush lansoprazole. Take it before a meal. Antacids may be taken with lansoprazole if needed. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Lansoprazole is not for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on 1 tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without chewing. Do not mix with other foods. If given through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow your healthcare provider’s instructions. Special Populations Lansoprazole SoluTabs contain phenylalanine, which may not be suitable for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). Children under 1 year of age may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider if your child is under 1 year old. Always inform your healthcare provider about your health conditions and all medications or supplements you are taking to ensure lansoprazole is safe and effective for you.
